cloud-computing.summary: A practical, beginner-friendly cloud computing certificate course in {city}: cloud service models, virtual machines, storage, networking, security and deployment, practised hands-on on real cloud platforms. No advanced coding background needed.
overview: The Cloud Computing Certificate Course in {city} is a practical, career-focused programme for students and professionals who want to build skills in one of the fastest-growing areas of IT. Cloud computing powers the apps, websites, storage and business systems that companies use every day, which makes these skills useful across many industries.

The course introduces cloud fundamentals in simple, beginner-friendly steps — service models (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS), virtual machines, storage, networking basics, security fundamentals, and how organisations deploy and manage services online. The emphasis is on hands-on practice, so you understand how cloud platforms work in real workplace situations. It suits 12th-pass students, graduates, job seekers and working professionals who want to move into IT roles or upgrade their technical profile.
cloud-computing.syllabusIntro: Seven modules that take you from what the cloud is to launching, securing and monitoring services on a real platform — and documenting the work like a professional.

modules.title: Cloud Fundamentals
points: What cloud computing is, and how it differs from traditional on-premise IT
Why businesses adopt the cloud
Service models: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS
Deployment models: public, private and hybrid cloud
Core terms: scalability, availability and pay-as-you-go pricing

modules.title: Virtual Machines and Compute
points: Creating and configuring virtual servers
Starting, stopping and monitoring instances
Compute resources: CPU, memory and operating systems
How applications actually run in the cloud

modules.title: Cloud Storage and Databases
points: Object and file storage
Backups and data lifecycle basics
Introduction to cloud databases
Organising and protecting stored data

modules.title: Networking Basics
points: IP addresses and DNS
Firewalls and virtual networks
How traffic moves between users and cloud services
The networking foundation of cloud administration and IT support

modules.title: Security and Access Management
points: Identity and access management (IAM) essentials
Passwords and multi-factor authentication
User roles and permissions
The shared responsibility model

modules.title: Deployment, Monitoring and Cost Awareness
points: Deploying simple applications and websites
Monitoring performance
Avoiding unnecessary cloud costs
Cost management as a practical, employable skill

modules.title: Workplace and Documentation Skills
points: Word: reports, documentation and standard operating procedures
Excel: formulas, sorting, filters and charts for tracking resources, usage and costs
PowerPoint: presenting a project or architecture idea clearly
Outlook: professional email, calendars and team communication

role.title: Cloud Support Associate
role.text: You will be able to explain cloud concepts in plain language, launch and manage a virtual server, store and secure data, and handle networking and access-control basics — the groundwork for cloud support, technical support, IT helpdesk and junior systems roles, and for vendor fundamentals certifications.

tools.name: AWS
tools.text: EC2 virtual machines, S3 storage, IAM users and the free-tier console.

tools.name: Microsoft Azure
tools.text: Virtual machines, storage accounts and resource groups in the Azure portal.

tools.name: Google Cloud
tools.text: Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and the Google Cloud console.

tools.name: Linux
tools.text: The command line, file permissions, packages and services on cloud servers.

tools.name: Windows
tools.text: Setting up Windows machines, users and remote administration.

tools.name: SSH
tools.text: Key-based login and secure remote access to Linux servers.

tools.name: Remote Desktop
tools.text: Connecting to and managing Windows machines in the cloud.

tools.name: Cloud Consoles & Dashboards
tools.text: Monitoring, billing alerts and cost dashboards across providers.

tools.name: Basic Scripting
tools.text: Small scripts that automate setup and routine admin tasks.

tools.name: Microsoft Office
tools.text: Documentation, reports and architecture notes for your projects.

flutter-app-development.summary: Build Android and iOS apps from a single codebase. This Flutter app development course in {city} moves from Dart fundamentals to UI, state management, APIs, Firebase and Play Store publishing, and ends with a capstone app for your portfolio.
overview: The Flutter App Development Course in {city} is designed for learners who want to build modern mobile apps for Android and iOS from a single codebase. Flutter is Google's open-source UI toolkit; it uses the Dart language and is widely used by startups and software companies for fast cross-platform development.

The course follows how apps are built at work: from Dart fundamentals to UI building, state management, backend integration with Firebase and finally app release, so each topic builds on the one before. It is open to 12th-pass students, graduates, job seekers, working professionals and freelancers — you need curiosity and regular practice, not a computer science degree.
flutter-app-development.syllabusIntro: Eleven modules, each ending with a clear outcome, that take you from your first Dart program to an app published on the Play Store.

modules.title: Programming and Dart Fundamentals
points: Variables, data types, operators, conditions, loops and functions
Null safety and collections: lists, sets and maps
Classes, inheritance and mixins
Asynchronous programming with Future, async/await and Streams
Outcome: write clean Dart programs and understand how object-oriented code is structured

modules.title: Flutter Setup and Core Widgets
points: Installing the Flutter SDK and setting up Android Studio or VS Code
Running apps on an emulator
The widget tree, StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget
Text, Image, Container, Row, Column, Stack, ListView and GridView
Outcome: build static app screens and understand how Flutter renders them

modules.title: Layouts, Theming and Responsive Design
points: Constraints, padding and alignment
MediaQuery and LayoutBuilder
Themes, custom fonts and Material 3 design
Screens that adapt to different phone sizes and orientations
Outcome: turn a design, such as a Figma screen, into a clean, responsive interface

modules.title: Navigation, Forms and User Input
points: Navigator and named routes
Declarative routing with go_router
Forms with validation, text fields, dropdowns, date pickers and dialogs
Outcome: build multi-screen apps with login, signup and input flows

modules.title: State Management
points: Starting with setState
Provider and Riverpod
Introduction to Bloc and Cubit
Choosing the right approach for each app
Outcome: organise app data and logic so apps stay maintainable as they grow

modules.title: Working with APIs and Data
points: Calling REST APIs with http or Dio
Parsing JSON and handling loading and error states
Displaying dynamic lists
Local storage with SharedPreferences, Hive and SQLite (sqflite)
Outcome: build apps that fetch live data and work with saved data

modules.title: Firebase Integration
points: Authentication: email, phone OTP and Google sign-in
Cloud Firestore databases
Firebase Storage for files
Push notifications with Firebase Cloud Messaging
Outcome: a complete app with user accounts, a cloud database and notifications, without writing your own backend

modules.title: Device Features and Animations
points: Camera, gallery, location and maps
Permissions and URL launching
Implicit and explicit animations and hero transitions
Basic custom painting
Outcome: add polish and native-like features to your apps

modules.title: Testing, Debugging and Performance
points: Flutter DevTools
Unit, widget and basic integration testing
Reading error logs
Spotting performance issues such as unnecessary rebuilds
Outcome: find and fix bugs and write more reliable code

modules.title: Git, Release and Publishing
points: Version control with Git and GitHub
App signing and build flavours
Generating APK and App Bundle files
Publishing to the Google Play Store
iOS publishing, introduced conceptually (it needs a Mac and an Apple Developer account)
Outcome: take an app from your laptop to a store listing

modules.title: Capstone Project and Portfolio
points: A complete project: an e-commerce, food delivery, task manager or learning app
A GitHub profile that shows your work
A short project walkthrough for interviews
Outcome: a showcase project and a portfolio to present to employers

projects.title: Capstone App
projects.text: A complete app of your choice — e-commerce, food delivery, task manager or learning app — with a GitHub repository and an interview walkthrough.

projects.title: Firebase-Powered App
projects.text: User accounts with email, phone OTP or Google sign-in, a Cloud Firestore database, file storage and push notifications.

projects.title: Live-Data App
projects.text: An app that calls a REST API, parses JSON, handles loading and error states, and caches data locally for offline use.

role.title: Junior Flutter Developer
role.text: With a solid portfolio you can apply for junior Flutter developer, mobile app developer, cross-platform developer and app tester roles — or freelance, building catalogue, booking and delivery apps for small businesses in {city} and nearby cities.

tools.name: Flutter
tools.text: Widgets, layouts, navigation, theming and state management.

tools.name: Dart
tools.text: Variables, classes, async/await and null safety — the language behind Flutter.

tools.name: pub.dev Packages
tools.text: Finding and adding packages for HTTP, storage, maps and more.

tools.name: Android Studio
tools.text: Project setup, the SDK manager and Android builds.

tools.name: VS Code
tools.text: The everyday editor, with the Flutter and Dart extensions.

tools.name: Android Emulator
tools.text: Running and testing your apps on virtual devices.

tools.name: Flutter DevTools
tools.text: Inspecting widgets, debugging and profiling performance.

tools.name: Xcode
tools.text: iOS builds and the iPhone simulator on macOS.

tools.name: Firebase
tools.text: Authentication, the Firestore database and push notifications.

tools.name: Postman
tools.text: Testing REST APIs before wiring them into your app.

tools.name: Git & GitHub
tools.text: Version control, commits and publishing your portfolio.

tools.name: Figma
tools.text: Reading app designs and turning screens into widgets.
